decks.notes: This deck focuses on utilizing a variety of powerful control cards, such as counterspells, removal, and card draw, to outmaneuver and disrupt the opponent's game plan. It also seeks to generate incremental advantage through the companion Lurrus of the Dream-Den, allowing for additional value over the course of a game. With a combination of disruption, card advantage, and a proactive game plan, this Dimir Control deck aims to control the tempo of the game and ultimately emerge victorious through careful manipulation of resources and strategic decision-making.

The deck focuses on using powerful card draw and control elements to support a combo win condition. It includes disruption cards like Force of Will and Swords to Plowshares to protect the combo pieces, along with mana acceleration from Moxen and other artifacts. The combo involves playing cards like Doorkeeper Thrull, Phyrexian Dreadnought, and Nulldrifter to create a game-winning board state. The deck aims to efficiently assemble and execute the combo while maintaining enough control over the game to prevent opponents from stopping it.

The deck focuses on utilizing control elements to disrupt the opponent's strategy while leveraging the graveyard as a resource through cards like Gifts Ungiven and Underworld Breach. It seeks to outvalue the opponent by efficiently casting spells and generating card advantage through powerful draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Gitaxian Probe. The inclusion of powerful mana acceleration like Black Lotus and Moxen enables the deck to cast powerful spells earlier in the game. Additionally, the deck can use Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion to further enhance its graveyard interactions and generate incremental value over time.

This deck focuses on putting aggressive creatures on the board while disrupting the opponent with hate cards like Chalice of the Void, Trinisphere, and Wasteland. The goal is to slow down the opponent's game plan with cards like Archon of Emeria and Chancellor of the Annex, while also generating card advantage with Seasoned Dungeoneer and Witch Enchanter. The deck aims to control the board and limit the opponent's options while steadily chipping away at their life total with efficient creatures like White Plume Adventurer and Clarion Conqueror.

The deck focuses on quickly filling the graveyard with cards like Stinkweed Imp and Golgari Thug, triggering powerful combo effects with cards like Narcomoeba and Prized Amalgam. Using Bazaar of Baghdad and Serum Powder, the deck can dig for key pieces and set up for explosive turns. The deck also includes disruption like Force of Will and Mindbreak Trap to protect its combo. By efficiently utilizing the graveyard and powerful synergies, the deck aims to overwhelm opponents with a fast and resilient combo strategy.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's resources and slowing them down with cards like Wasteland, Sphere of Resistance, and Null Rod, while also ramping up quickly with cards like Mishra's Workshop and Ancient Tomb. It utilizes artifact creatures like Nettlecyst and Patchwork Automaton to apply pressure early on, and has access to powerful utility lands like Tolarian Academy and Inventors' Fair. The deck also includes cards like Karn, the Great Creator and Mystic Forge for additional versatility and card advantage. Overall, the deck aims to overwhelm the opponent with efficient threats and disruptive elements.

The deck focuses on disrupting the opponent's strategy with hate cards like Chalice of the Void, Trinisphere, and Chancellor of the Annex, while deploying aggressive creatures like Archon of Emeria and Anointed Peacekeeper to apply pressure. The deck uses efficient mana sources like Moxen and Ancient Tomb to power out its threats quickly, and includes disruptive lands like Karakas and Wasteland to control the opponent's board. The deck aims to restrict opponent's options while maintaining a steady stream of threats to close out the game quickly.

The deck focuses on controlling the game using counterspells and removal while also utilizing the powerful ability of Oath of Druids to cheat out big threats like Atraxa, Grand Unifier. It also includes a mix of card draw and manipulation to maintain card advantage and find key pieces. The inclusion of powerful planeswalkers like Oko, Thief of Crowns and Wrenn and Six adds versatility and additional threats to the deck. Overall, the strategy revolves around disrupting the opponent's game plan while establishing a strong board presence with efficient threats.

This deck focuses on using efficient control spells and powerful card advantage engines to disrupt the opponent's game plan while setting up its win condition. By leveraging powerful artifacts like Time Vault and Bolas's Citadel, along with extra turns and card draw from cards like Time Walk and Narset, Parter of Veils, it aims to outvalue the opponent and secure victory through a combination of attrition and powerful combo finishes. The deck also includes disruptive elements like Force of Will and Opposition Agent to further disrupt the opponent's plans while maintaining its own game plan.

This deck focuses on utilizing control elements to disrupt the opponent's game plan while drawing cards and generating advantage through various spells and abilities. By efficiently managing resources and using countermagic, removal, and card draw, the deck aims to control the pace of the game and outvalue the opponent. The inclusion of cards like Lurrus of the Dream-Den and Ancestral Recall allows for additional flexibility and card advantage, while the deck's mana base and powerful spells provide stability and consistency in executing its game plan.

The deck aims to disrupt the opponent's strategy by playing hatebears such as Chancellor of the Annex, Archon of Emeria, and Anointed Peacekeeper while also applying pressure with aggressive creatures like Clarion Conqueror and Seasoned Dungeoneer. It leverages powerful mana acceleration with artifacts like Black Lotus and Moxen to quickly deploy threats onto the battlefield. The deck also utilizes disruptive lands like Wasteland and Strip Mine to further hinder the opponent's resources. The combination of hatebears, aggressive creatures, and mana acceleration makes it a formidable aggro-hatebear deck in Vintage 1 vs 1 format.

This deck focuses on utilizing the combo potential of Paradoxical Outcome to generate a large amount of mana and card advantage through cards such as Moxen, Mana Vault, and Time Walk. By efficiently cycling through the deck with cards like Ancestral Recall and Brainstorm, the deck aims to assemble a winning combination quickly while disrupting the opponent's game plan with counter magic like Force of Will and Pyroblast. Additionally, the inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value and resilience in the late game.

The deck focuses on maintaining control over the game by disrupting the opponent's strategy with counterspells and removal, while establishing a strong board presence with efficient creatures. Key cards like Force of Will, Swords to Plowshares, and Lavinia, Azorius Renegade help to control the game, while powerful draw spells like Ancestral Recall and Dig Through Time provide card advantage. The addition of a companion in Lurrus of the Dream-Den allows for additional resilience and flexibility in the deck's strategy, making it a formidable control archetype in Vintage 1 vs 1 format.

The deck focuses on utilizing hatebears and aggressive creatures to disrupt opponents' game plans while quickly closing out the game. By combining efficient disruptive elements like Thalia, Guardian of Thraben and Archon of Emeria with aggressive creatures like Clarion Conqueror and White Plume Adventurer, the deck aims to slow down the opponent's strategy while applying pressure on the board. The deck also includes cards like Deafening Silence and Anointed Peacekeeper to further disrupt opponents' spellcasting and combat phases, creating a challenging board state for the opponent to navigate.

This deck revolves around assembling the combo pieces needed to win the game with Thassa's Oracle as quickly as possible. It includes various cantrips, disruption spells, and efficient mana sources to help dig for and protect the combo. The goal is to utilize Doomsday to stack the top of the library with the necessary cards and win the game in a single turn with Thassa's Oracle. The deck is built for speed and efficiency, aiming to outpace and outmaneuver the opponent to achieve victory.

The main focus of this deck is to maintain control of the game while applying pressure to the opponent with efficient creatures and disruptive spells. By utilizing a strong mix of countermagic, removal, and powerful creatures like Deathrite Shaman and Dauthi Voidwalker, the deck aims to disrupt the opponent's game plan while establishing a clock to quickly close out the game. The inclusion of Lurrus of the Dream-Den as a companion provides additional value and recursion to keep the pressure on the opponent. Overall, the deck is built to be versatile and adaptable in various matchups.
